description: How a byte count is shown. Decimal units, matching Finder and the limits upload sites quote: 1 MB is 1,000,000 bytes.
rounding: half up - floor(x + 0.5). Python's round() rounds half to even and must not be used here.

cases.why: never show '0 KB' for a real file
the case where banker's rounding would say 2 KB
still KB just below the MB boundary
one decimal place from here up

typed.description: Reading a size the user typed into the 'Max file size' box. A bare number means KB, since that is the unit upload limits are usually quoted in. Anything that cannot be read must be refused, so the field can be marked wrong, rather than guessed at.
typed.note: Only the two front ends parse typed sizes; the Python server receives an integer byte count. Both front ends implement this in JavaScript, and the macOS app's copy is inline in src/convertly/web/index.html pending consolidation onto web/js/sizes.js.

accepted.why: spacing and case do not matter
a bare number is KB, so this is 900,000 KB

refused.why: a limit of nothing cannot be met
under 1 KB is never achievable, so it is a mistake
not a unit this understands; guessing would be worse
two decimal points. This used to be read as 1.2 MB, silently applying a limit nobody asked for
